artists.biography:
Crowded House are a pop rock band formed in Melbourne, Australia in 1985 by lead-vocalist and primary songwriter, New Zealand-born Neil Finn. Other members have included his brother Tim Finn, Australians Paul Hester, Nick Seymour and Peter Jones and Americans Mark Hart and Matt Sherrod.
Crowded House has won several national and international awards. In Australia, the group has won eleven ARIA Awards from 26 nominations, including the inaugural Best New Talent award in 1987. The majority of their ARIAs were awarded for their first two albums, Crowded House and Temple of Low Men. They won eight APRA Awards from eleven nominations and were nominated for The New Zealand Silver Scroll for "Don't Stop Now" in 2007.
"Don't Dream It's Over" was named the seventh best Australian song of all time in 2001.

perplexity.description:
Intriguer is the sixth studio album by Crowded House, released on 11 June 2010. The album marked the band's second release following their 2007 reunion, featuring the lineup of Neil Finn on vocals, guitars and piano, founding member Nick Seymour on bass guitar, Mark Hart on guitars and keyboards, and Matt Sherrod on drums. Recorded across multiple studios between April 2009 and January 2010—including Roundhead Studios in Auckland, RAK Studios in London, and Real World Studios in Wiltshire—the album was produced by Jim Scott and showcases the band's alternative rock sensibilities.

The album demonstrates Crowded House's mature approach to pop-rock songwriting, balancing the band's signature melodic craftsmanship with contemporary production. At 40 minutes in length, Intriguer contains ten tracks that reflect the group's established style of adult alternative pop/rock. The opening single "Saturday Sun" was released to radio in April 2010, establishing the album's commercial trajectory.

Critical reception was decidedly mixed. While Q Magazine awarded three stars and noted that the album represented "his best work in nearly two decades," other reviewers were less enthusiastic. Uncut similarly gave three stars but criticized the record for retreating "into tastefulness," a perceived weakness in Crowded House's approach. The Guardian's Ally Carnwath also assigned three stars, suggesting that the album's more conventionally structured pop songs "invariably sound dull". Despite the divided critical response, Intriguer solidified Crowded House's position as a continuing force in alternative rock following their successful reunion.
